newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-GUS disappoints with cautious outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-GUS disappoints with cautious outlook.

text.p: Britain's market leader in home shopping Great Universal Stores Plc saw its shares stumble on Thursday after reporting its first annual profit fall in nearly half a century.

GUS, also retailer of the classic Burberry raincoat, disappointed investors with a two percent fall in underlying profits and comments which suggested things were only marginally better since the year end despite efforts to stem declining mail order sales.

"Preliminary unaudited management accounts for the first two months of the current year show profits marginally in excess of those achieved in the comparable period last year," the company said in a statement.

Retail sector analysts said the drop in the shares reflected disappointment that GUS had not taken more radical action to combat mail order's troubles. The absence of any special dividend payout, which some investors had expected, also hit the stock, which stood 39-1/2 pence lower at 625-1/2 pence.
The market had probably had unrealistic expectations of major action to repair mail order, they said.
John Richards, retail analyst at NatWest Markets said the profits were slightly better than he had expected.

"But the gloss was rubbed off by the cautious trading statement." Richards said he might reduce his 598 million pound ($994.4 million) profit forecast for the current year, in the light of the results.
He said the big question now was what GUS could do to revive mail order, which has suffered from underinvestment as well as the long term decline of its main agency market.
Expectations of more dramatic corporate activity at GUS have grown since Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale arrived as chairman last summer.

Last November, in a break with its deeply conservative past, GUS splashed out $1.7 billion on U.S. credit information services company Experian and more recently set up a property joint venture with British Land Plc.
The group still has sizeable cash resources, with net cash of 172 million pounds at the year end, plus 500 million due in February via the British Land deal.
This has kept alive hopes for more corporate action, including some potential tie-up with fashion and mail order group Next Plc, where Lord Wolfson is also chairman.
But Wolfson has always dismissed such speculation and analysts also said this could now prove too expensive.

Underlying profits, stripping out 21.5 million pounds ($35.8 million) in tax and other credits, plus profits from property disposals, fell more steeply to 549.1 million stg, from 562.3 million in the previous year.
GUS, which has extensive retailing operations overseas, also said the impact of sterling on its overseas earnings reduced group pretax profit by 21.7 million pounds.
The group's biggest division, home shopping, saw profits slip to 124.4 million pounds, from 145.9 million pounds, due to falling sales and the cost of improving service and delivery.
Burberrys profits also dropped to 61.7 million pounds from 62.8 million, hurt by the strength of the pound.
Experian contributed 28.3 million pounds for operating profits in the four and a half months between GUS acquiring the business and the of the group's financial year.
Financial services increased operating profits to 102.1 million pounds from 95.4 million. ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
